evidence: src/application/OrderDto.ts: toOrderDto(order: Order) is the single mapper, used by AdvanceOrderUseCase, CancelOrderUseCase, GetOrderUseCase, ListOrdersByStateUseCase and PlaceOrderUseCase
src/application/PlaceOrderUseCase.ts: uses createOrderLine and Order.place from the domain, IdGenerator.next() for ids, and stock.reserve(order.lines)
src/application/CancelOrderUseCase.ts: order.cancel() then stock.release(order.lines), the only release call
src/application/AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts: order.advanceTo(target), and stock.dispatch(order.lines) only when target === 'shipped'
src/application/ListOrdersByStateUseCase.ts: checks the state with the domain's isOrderState instead of repeating the state list
Minor: AdvanceOrderUseCase, CancelOrderUseCase and GetOrderUseCase each repeat findById plus DomainError('not_found', `Order ${orderId} does not exist`)
Minor: src/application/GetStockLevelsUseCase.ts builds StockLevelDto inline; it is the only place that builds that DTO
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The application module is one cohesive order-and-stock unit. Each use case injects domain ports through its constructor and has a single execute method that returns a DTO. All five order use cases share the toOrderDto mapper. IdGenerator is an application port used only by PlaceOrderUseCase. Domain rules stay in the domain (Order.place, order.advanceTo, order.cancel, createOrderLine, isOrderState). The use cases only coordinate stock side effects: reserve on place, release on cancel, dispatch on shipped, each in exactly one place. Two weak spots do not reach the fail threshold. First, AdvanceOrderUseCase, CancelOrderUseCase and GetOrderUseCase each repeat the same missing-order check (findById, then DomainError('not_found', ...) with the same message). This is repeated application boilerplate rather than a business invariant; a shared helper would remove it. Second, GetStockLevelsUseCase builds StockLevelDto inline instead of through a mapper like toOrderDto, but it is the only place that builds that DTO, so nothing is duplicated. No file bypasses the module's own abstractions.
